# Tool screen: ERPNext / Frappe Framework

**Question set:** seven-question integration-gap screen for Powerhouse
**Researched:** 2026-08-19 · primary sources only · by knowledge-agent
**Scope note:** ERPNext (the ERP application) and Frappe Framework (the platform beneath it) are
**separately licensed** and are treated separately below where it matters.

---

## LEAD: corporate status in the last 24 months

Frappe is an **acquirer, not a target**. Frappe Technologies acquired **The Commit Company on 1 January
2026**, with the team joining Frappe and "all existing products and libraries being moved to the Frappe
GitHub repository."
Source: https://thecommit.company/blog/company/announcing-our-acquisition-by-frappe

No relicensing or archival found. This resolves — in the opposite direction — an unverified "acquisition
lead" raised earlier in this research.

---

## 1. WHAT IT DOES KEEP

Frappe maintains change history in the **`Version` DocType**. When `track_changes` is enabled on a DocType,
every save creates a Version record capturing "the additions, deletions, and modifications made during that
specific save instance."
Source: https://docs.frappe.io/erpnext/user/manual/en/document-versioning

Alongside it sit ordinary logging DocTypes — Error Log, Activity Log, Route History — governed by a
**Log Settings** DocType which "lets you configure retention period for default logging doctypes."
Source: https://docs.frappe.io/framework/user/en/logging

**Storage form:** all of these are ordinary DocTypes, i.e. **rows in the relational database**
(`tabVersion` etc.). They are not an append-only stream and carry no documented hash or chain.

---

## 2. WHAT IT DOES NOT KEEP — the gap

**There is no immutable, user-attributed, append-only log of business events on by default.** Four
independent findings:

**(a) Tracking is opt-in, per DocType.** Versioning is enabled by ticking "Track changes" in Customize Form:
> "Go to Purchase Order List. Click on Customize from the drop-down menu... Check the field 'Track changes'
> in the Properties."
Source: https://docs.frappe.io/erpnext/user/manual/en/document-versioning
A business event on an untracked DocType leaves no Version record at all.

**(b) Deleting the document destroys its history — the decisive finding.** On delete, Frappe removes the
document's Version references:
> `delete_references("Version", doctype, name, "ref_doctype", "docname")`
Source: https://github.com/frappe/frappe/blob/develop/frappe/model/delete_doc.py
**The audit trail dies with the record it audits.** An append-only log must outlive its subject; this one
does not.

**(c) Records are mutable rows.** Version entries are ordinary DocType rows in MariaDB/Postgres, reachable by
`frappe.delete_doc` (the document `delete()` method "is an alias to `frappe.delete_doc`",
https://frappeframework.com/docs/user/en/api/document) and by any direct SQL `UPDATE`. Nothing in the
documentation asserts immutability, hashing or tamper-evidence.

**(d) Retention is a pruning system by design.** "Most logging doctypes in Frappe support configurable
retention period with sane defaults", cleared on a scheduled basis.
Source: https://docs.frappe.io/framework/user/en/logging

**Paid gating:** none found. The capability is not withheld behind a paid tier — it simply is not an
append-only business log. This is a design boundary, not an upsell.

**UNVERIFIED:** the exact numeric default retention for each logging DocType (the docs say "sane defaults"
without listing them; a 180-day figure appears only as a code example for *custom* logging doctypes);
whether `Version` is itself registered for automatic clearing by default; and whether Frappe Cloud offers
any audit capability beyond the self-hosted product.

---

## 3. IS THE SLOT ALREADY OCCUPIED?

**No — not for this gap.** Frappe does ship a first-party feature literally called **Audit Trail**, so this
required checking. It is narrower than its name:
> "A tool for viewing the changes made to a submittable doctype across multiple amended versions" — tracking
> "Fields Changed", "Rows Updated", "Rows Added / Rows Removed".
Source: https://docs.frappe.io/framework/user/en/audit-trail

That is a **diff viewer over amendments of submittable documents**, not an immutable attributed log of
business decisions. The page makes no claim of default-on behaviour, immutability, hashing, chaining or
deletion protection. No vendor announcement in the last 24 months was found that closes the gap — the one
material corporate event is Frappe *acquiring* a developer-tooling company (see LEAD).

No sovereignty wedge is required, because the slot is open.

---

## 4. LICENCE REALITY

Two repositories, two licences — the distinction matters:

| component | licence (as stated in the repo) | source |
|---|---|---|
| **ERPNext** (application) | **GPL-3.0** | https://github.com/frappe/erpnext |
| **Frappe Framework** (platform) | **MIT** | https://github.com/frappe/frappe |

Both are genuine OSI-approved open source. **No open-core split was found on the audit capability** — unlike
the open-core vendors elsewhere in this corpus, there is no Enterprise edition withholding the audit feature.
GPL-3.0 on ERPNext is copyleft and reciprocal, which is compatible with Powerhouse's own AGPL-3.0 posture and
unproblematic for public-sector procurement. MIT on the framework is permissive.

No discrepancy found between vendor FAQ and repo.

---

## 5. INSTALL BASE — order of magnitude

- **ERPNext: 38.3k GitHub stars** (github.com/frappe/erpnext, retrieved 2026-08-19)
- **Frappe Framework: 10.6k GitHub stars** (github.com/frappe/frappe, retrieved 2026-08-19)

**Order of magnitude: 10⁴ stars**, placing it among the larger open-source business platforms in this corpus.

**UNVERIFIED:** Docker pull counts, published customer numbers and partner-directory size were not retrieved.

---

## 6. THE INTEGRATION SEAM

**`doc_events` in `hooks.py`** — a documented, first-class controller-hook mechanism, with wildcard support
across all DocTypes:

```python
doc_events = {
    "*": {
        "after_insert": "app.crud_events.after_insert_all"
    },
    "ToDo": {
        "before_insert": "app.crud_events.before_insert_todo",
    }
}
```
Source: https://docs.frappe.io/framework/user/en/python-api/hooks

"The method will be passed the doc and the method name as arguments." Lifecycle events include
`after_insert`, `before_insert`, `on_update`, `on_submit`, `on_cancel`.

This is an unusually good seam: the `"*"` wildcard means a single hook registration can dispatch a typed
operation for **every** business document in the system, without touching individual DocTypes.

---

## 7. THE DEMO SCENARIO

**a) Dispatch a typed operation at the decision point.** Register `doc_events` on `on_submit` for
Purchase Order (or Sales Invoice). Submitting the document — the moment of business approval — dispatches a
typed, user-attributed operation to Powerhouse recording who submitted it, when, and the state at submission.

**b) Destroy the record in ERPNext.** Delete the Purchase Order. Frappe's `delete_doc` cascades
`delete_references("Version", doctype, name, ...)`, so the document **and its entire version history**
disappear together. Optionally also demonstrate mutation: a direct `UPDATE` on `tabVersion` alters the
"audit" record silently, since it is an ordinary row.

**c) Replay the business decision from Powerhouse.** The append-only record still answers who approved the
purchase order, when, and under which rule.

**What the viewer sees in under 60 seconds:** the approval exists in ERPNext; the document is deleted; ERPNext
can no longer answer *who approved it* — the version history went with the record — while Powerhouse replays
the approval chain intact. The point being proved is not that ERPNext is careless, but that **its history is
scoped to the lifetime of the row**, and a decision record must outlive the thing it describes.

---

## VERDICT ROW (notion-tools.csv)

```
tool | slot | verdict | licence | origin | role_in_stack | why_it_matters | install_base | demo_scenario | evidence_urls
```

**ERPNext / Frappe** | open — no first-party append-only business log; the shipped "Audit Trail" is an
amendment diff viewer only | **PRIMARY** | ERPNext GPL-3.0; Frappe Framework MIT — both OSI, no open-core
gating of audit | Frappe Technologies (India); acquirer of The Commit Company Jan-2026; no relicensing |
ERP / system of record for transactions, with change history scoped to the row's lifetime | Version records
are opt-in per DocType, are mutable database rows, are subject to configurable pruning, and are **deleted
with the document they audit** (`delete_references("Version", ...)`) — so ERPNext cannot answer "who approved
this" once the record is gone | ~38.3k GitHub stars (ERPNext) + ~10.6k (Frappe), retrieved 2026-08-19; order
of magnitude 10⁴ | `doc_events` hook on `on_submit` of Purchase Order dispatches a typed operation → delete
the Purchase Order in ERPNext, cascading deletion of its Version history → replay the approval chain from
Powerhouse | https://github.com/frappe/erpnext · https://github.com/frappe/frappe ·
https://github.com/frappe/frappe/blob/develop/frappe/model/delete_doc.py ·
https://docs.frappe.io/framework/user/en/python-api/hooks ·
https://docs.frappe.io/framework/user/en/audit-trail ·
https://docs.frappe.io/framework/user/en/logging ·
https://docs.frappe.io/erpnext/user/manual/en/document-versioning ·
https://frappeframework.com/docs/user/en/api/document ·
https://thecommit.company/blog/company/announcing-our-acquisition-by-frappe

---

## Remaining tools — NOT RESEARCHED

Flowable, Odoo, Alfresco, n8n and Camunda were commissioned but **halted before any screen completed.**
No verdicts exist for them. Open hypotheses for whoever resumes:

- **Odoo** — is the Audit Trail app Community or Enterprise? If Enterprise-only and proprietary, that is
  itself the sovereignty wedge.
- **n8n** — the `EXECUTIONS_DATA_PRUNE` default, and whether the Sustainable Use Licence qualifies as open
  source for public procurement (it is not OSI-approved).
- **Alfresco** — whether auditing is on by default (`alfresco-audit-access.xml` was located in the Community
  repo; contents unconfirmed), and whether Governance Services already occupies the slot.
- **Camunda** — verify the premise that Camunda IDP (Aug 2025) + the ABBYY partnership (Dec 2025) closed this
  gap; plus Camunda 7 EOL and what Camunda 8's licence permits self-managed.
- **Flowable** — verify or refute the vault's existing claim that history is purgeable and the instance is a
  mutable row.

The vault's current claims about these five tools come from the lead workbook, **not** from primary sources,
and remain unverified.

---
---

# Tool screen: n8n

**Researched:** 2026-08-20 · primary sources only
**Verdict: PRIMARY** — with two independent wedges (technical gap + procurement licence)

## LEAD: corporate status
No relicensing, no acquisition. Live `LICENSE.md` still reads "Sustainable Use License / Version 1.0"
(created 2022, unchanged). Independent, Berlin HQ.
*UNVERIFIED-primary (secondary press only): $180M Series C at $2.5B post-money, Oct 2025; >$40M ARR;
3,000+ enterprise customers.*

## 1. WHAT IT KEEPS
Two ordinary TypeORM SQL tables. `execution_entity` holds metadata (`id`, `status`, `mode`, `createdAt`,
`startedAt`) and imports `DeleteDateColumn` — soft delete. `execution_data` holds the payload as **a single
`text` blob**, cascade-deleted with its parent:
```ts
@Column('text') data: string;
@OneToOne('ExecutionEntity', 'executionData', { onDelete: 'CASCADE' })
```
Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/n8n-io/n8n/master/packages/@n8n/db/src/entities/execution-data.ts ·
.../execution-entity.ts

Event log file: "By default, n8n writes the event log to `<n8n-user-folder>/n8nEventLog.log`"
— https://docs.n8n.io/administer/observe-and-log/stream-logs-to-external-systems.md

## 2. THE GAP — decisive: it forgets by default
**Being fair first:** `EXECUTIONS_DATA_SAVE_ON_SUCCESS` defaults to `all`, so n8n *does* record runs. The gap
is that it then **deletes them on a timer**, and what it records is not a business record.

| variable | **shipped default** |
|---|---|
| `EXECUTIONS_DATA_PRUNE` | **`true`** |
| `EXECUTIONS_DATA_MAX_AGE` | **`336` hours = 14 days** |
| `EXECUTIONS_DATA_PRUNE_MAX_COUNT` | `10000` |
| `EXECUTIONS_DATA_MAX_DISPLAY_SIZE` | `104857600` (100 MB, truncates display) |

> "n8n enables pruning by default" … prunes when **either** "**Age**: The execution finished more than
> `EXECUTIONS_DATA_MAX_AGE` hours ago" or the count exceeds `PRUNE_MAX_COUNT`, removing "finished executions
> along with their execution data and binary data."
— https://docs.n8n.io/deploy/host-n8n/configure-n8n/scaling/manage-execution-data ·
https://docs.n8n.io/deploy/host-n8n/configure-n8n/basic-configuration/use-environment-variables/executions

**Deletion API:** `DELETE /api/v1/executions/{id}` — "Deletes an execution from your instance."
https://docs.n8n.io/connect/n8n-api/execution.md

**Mutability:** ordinary Postgres/SQLite/MySQL rows behind TypeORM. No hash, no signature, no chain, no
append-only constraint in either entity. Anyone with DB credentials can `UPDATE execution_data SET data = ...`
undetected.

**No user attribution on the decision.** `mode` is an enum (`webhook`, `trigger`, `manual`, `cli`, `retry`).
An execution is attributed to a **workflow**, never to a deciding human under a rule.

**The `/audit` endpoint is not an audit log — it is a vulnerability scanner:**
> `"summary":"Generate an audit","description":"Generate a security audit for your n8n instance."` returning
> "Credentials Risk Report", "Database Risk Report", "Filesystem Risk Report", "Nodes Risk Report"
— https://docs.n8n.io/connect/n8n-api/audit.md

**Audit events that do exist are identity/admin only** — login, signup, credentials, MFA, package installed,
`User execution deleted`, `Execution data revealed`. Nothing about *what was decided*.

**Paid gating, stated twice independently:**
> "Log Streaming is available on: **n8n Cloud:** Enterprise • **Self-hosted:** Enterprise"
> "The Community edition … doesn't include these features: … Log streaming"
— https://docs.n8n.io/administer/observe-and-log/stream-logs-to-external-systems.md ·
https://docs.n8n.io/deploy/host-n8n/community-edition-features.md

Note the irony: **"User execution deleted" is itself only observable through the Enterprise-only channel.**

## 3. SLOT: not occupied for business-event provenance
n8n 2.x shipped adjacent-but-different features (https://docs.n8n.io/changelog/release-notes-2.x.md):
execution-data **redaction** (Enterprise — hides payloads, does not preserve them); **Insights** (aggregate
metrics only, "successes, failures, runtime, and time saved", Enterprise-gated, 365-day default retention);
**workflow version history** (versions the workflow *definition*, not business events); OAuth token exchange
(API-call attribution); **Data Tables** (mutable rows with insert/update/delete, no versioning).

Slot is open. Where partially occupied, the occupier is proprietary `.ee.` code behind a paid key — and it is
observability, not a ledger.

## 4. LICENCE REALITY — not OSI open source
Verbatim from live `LICENSE.md`:
> "You may use or modify the software only for your own internal business purposes or for non-commercial or
> personal use. You may distribute the software or provide it to others only if you do so free of charge for
> non-commercial purposes."

Plus a second proprietary tier in the same repo:
> "Source code files that contain \".ee.\" in their filename or \".ee\" in their dirname are NOT licensed under
> the Sustainable Use License."

- n8n's own README says "**Fair-code**" and "**Source Available**" — it never claims "open source" for itself.
- faircode.io: "**Fair-code is not a software license.**" … "is commercially restricted by its authors."
- **GitHub's licence detector returns `NOASSERTION`** (GitHub API, 2026-08-20) — not a recognised SPDX/OSI licence.

**n8n is honest about this**; the wedge is procurement rules, not misrepresentation.

**Sovereignty wedge (two effects):**
1. *Verified:* any EU/German tender requiring **OSI-approved** open source cannot count n8n.
2. *INFERENCE, needs a lawyer:* a Land running n8n as a **shared service for municipalities with cost
   recharge** collides with n8n's own stated prohibition on "hosting n8n and charging people money to access
   it" — precisely the shape of German public-sector IT consolidation.

Contrast: Powerhouse is AGPL-3.0 + commercial dual licence — OSI-approved, no field-of-use restriction.

## 5. INSTALL BASE — the largest in the corpus
- **~201,251 GitHub stars** (~2×10⁵), 60,243 forks — GitHub API, 2026-08-20
- **~249,094,773 Docker Hub pulls** of `n8nio/n8n` (~2.5×10⁸) — Docker Hub API v2, 2026-08-20

## 6. THE INTEGRATION SEAM — four unrestricted entry points
HTTP Request node · Webhook node · **Custom node API incl. private nodes** (`install-private-nodes`, nothing
must be published) · public REST API at `/api/v1` (`X-N8N-API-KEY`).
https://docs.n8n.io/connect/create-nodes/overview.md
Cleanest path: a private `n8n-nodes-powerhouse` node dispatching typed operations to Switchboard. n8n's docs
explicitly permit "Creating an n8n node for your product."

## 7. DEMO SCENARIO — two panes, ~45 seconds
**a)** In an invoice-approval workflow, after the `IF` node (`amount > €10,000 → approval required`), an HTTP
Request node dispatches `APPROVE_INVOICE { invoiceId, approverId, amount, ruleVersion, timestamp }`.
**b)** Destroy it: `curl -X DELETE -H "X-N8N-API-KEY: $KEY" http://localhost:5678/api/v1/executions/1847`
— then say the line: *"and if I hadn't, the shipped default `EXECUTIONS_DATA_PRUNE=true` with
`EXECUTIONS_DATA_MAX_AGE=336` would have done it for me in fourteen days."*
**c)** Powerhouse still holds operation #N: `APPROVE_INVOICE`, signer, timestamp, rule version, prior-state
hash. Click replay.

**What the viewer sees:** left pane `GET /api/v1/executions/1847` → **404 "The specified resource was not
found."** Right pane — same decision, still attributed, still replayable. **The automation forgot. The record
did not.**

---
---

# Tool screen: Camunda

**Researched:** 2026-08-20 · primary sources only
**Verdict: SOVEREIGN WEDGE ONLY** — but for a completely different reason than the brief assumed

## LEAD: the brief's premise is wrong, and two structural changes matter more

**The brief said Camunda closed this gap with Camunda IDP (Aug 2025) + an ABBYY partnership (Dec 2025).
Both events are real. Neither touches audit records.** This is a category error:

- **Camunda IDP** (8.7, Apr 2025): "Use artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) to identify,
  extract, and organize data from your **structured and unstructured documents**"
  — https://docs.camunda.io/docs/components/modeler/web-modeler/idp/ — i.e. OCR/LLM extraction from scanned PDFs.
- **ABBYY partnership** (published 19 Dec 2025): "ABBYY brings best-in-class Document AI—classification,
  extraction, validation" delivered as an ABBYY Vantage REST **connector**
  — https://camunda.com/blog/2025/12/abbyy-and-camunda-reliable-document-ai-for-agentic-processes/

"Document" in *Intelligent Document Processing* means a scanned invoice. "Document" in Powerhouse means a
typed, append-only state machine. **Anyone screening Camunda out on the IDP/ABBYY basis has screened it out
for the wrong reason.**

**What actually changed, and the brief never mentioned:**

1. **The Apache-2.0 edition is archived.** `camunda/camunda-bpm-platform` — GitHub API 2026-08-20:
   `{"archived": true, "license": "Apache-2.0", "stars": 4269, "forks": 1720}`. Verbatim:
   > "the final feature release for Camunda 7 (7.24) is still scheduled for **October 14, 2025**, and the
   > repository will be archived shortly after. After this date, **no further releases, including security
   > patches**, will be made for Camunda 7 Community Edition."
   — https://camunda.com/blog/2025/02/camunda-7-enterprise-end-of-life-extension/
   (Enterprise got an extension to April 2030 / 2032; Community did not.)

2. **The slot IS largely occupied — by the Camunda 8.9 User Operations Audit Log**, GA and shipped
   (`8.9.16` released 2026-08-14; audit-log follow-up epic closed 2026-03-10). It records who did what, when,
   to which entities, across process/identity/user-task domains, queryable via the Orchestration Cluster API.
   — https://docs.camunda.io/docs/apis-tools/orchestration-cluster-api-rest/specifications/search-user-task-audit-logs/
   · https://roadmap.camunda.com/c/269-user-operations-audit-log

## 4. LICENCE REALITY — the decisive section
Verbatim, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/camunda/camunda/main/licenses/CAMUNDA-LICENSE-1.0.txt:
> "the Licensor hereby grants You the … right to Use the Software … **only and limited to the Use in or for
> the purpose of Using the Software in Non-Production Environment**."
> "**You must purchase a commercial license** … **or You must refrain from Using the Software**."
> "**You may not move, change, disable, or circumvent the license key functionality.**"
> "**Non-Production Environment** means … development, staging, testing, quality assurance, demonstration, or
> evaluation purposes, and **not for any live or production systems**."

Apache-2.0 covers only the periphery — Java client, Spring Boot starter, **Exporter API**, Protocol, BPMN
Model API. GitHub detects `license: null` on `camunda/camunda`.

**The critical asymmetry: the integration seam is Apache-2.0; the engine behind it is not.** Powerhouse can
write a permissively licensed exporter, but the customer still needs a paid licence for the thing it exports
from.

**Net: the only Apache-2.0 Camunda is unpatched abandonware; the only maintained Camunda is
production-forbidden without payment.** For a BSI/NIS2-governed German public buyer, "unpatched since October
2025" and "a proprietary licence key we are contractually forbidden to disable" are each disqualifying in
different ways. **That is the sovereignty wedge — not IDP.**

## 1–2. WHAT IT KEEPS / THE GAP, per edition

**Camunda 7 — gap real, quotable, permanent.** Default history level is `AUDIT`. The decisive line:
> "Rows in this table are **updated** as variable instances are updated, meaning that **only the last value
> of a process variable will be available**."
— https://docs.camunda.org/manual/7.24/user-guide/process-engine/history/history-configuration/

Destructive in-place update, not an append-only log. Prior state is gone unless you opt up to `FULL` (which is
also where the User Operation Log — the only user-attributed part — lives, i.e. **off by default**).

Deletion is designed in:
> "**The history time to live is mandatory**, any deployment or re-deployment of any model resource (BPMN, DMN,
> CMMN) that contains a historyTimeToLive of null **will be prevented**."
— https://docs.camunda.org/manual/7.24/user-guide/process-engine/history/history-cleanup/

**Camunda 7.24 refuses to deploy a process model until you declare when its history will be destroyed.**

Explicit APIs: `HistoryService.deleteHistoricProcessInstance(id)` ("Deletes historic process instance along
with all historic activities, historic task and historic details"), `...IfExists`, and bulk
`deleteHistoricProcessInstancesAsync(query, reason)`. No hash chain, no tamper evidence.

**Camunda 8 — mostly closed.** Retention ships **disabled** (`retention.enabled: false`, `minimum-age: 30d`) —
a genuine point in Camunda's favour. Residual gaps: records are ordinary mutable Elasticsearch/OpenSearch
documents (integrity protection *absent* — INFERRED, no source claims one exists), and the 8.9 audit log is
"Eventually Consistent" per its own API spec, so not transactionally coupled to the decision it records.

## 5. INSTALL BASE (GitHub API, 2026-08-20)
- `camunda/camunda-bpm-platform` (C7): **4,269 stars / 1,720 forks — archived**
- `camunda/camunda` (C8): **4,253 stars / 813 forks** — active, `license: null`

Order of magnitude 10³. C7's 1,720 forks reflect a decade-long, now-frozen enterprise estate.
Partner directory exists at camunda.com/partners with Platinum/Gold/Silver tiers confirmed.
**The ~204 count is UNVERIFIED** (JS-rendered); the lead-corpus "advertises Gold but absent from directory"
claim therefore remains **UNVERIFIED** — feasible to check, needs a rendered-DOM pass.

## 6. THE INTEGRATION SEAM
- **C8: Exporter API (`zeebe/exporter-api`), Apache-2.0** — receives every record on the Zeebe stream. The
  cleanest seam, legally unencumbered on Powerhouse's side.
- **C7:** `JavaDelegate`, `ExecutionListener` (start/end/take), `TaskListener` (create/assignment/complete/
  delete). The `complete` event is where human identity actually exists.
- gRPC stubs generated from `gateway.proto` "does not constitute creating a derivative work under the Camunda
  License 1.0" — client-side integration is legally clean.

## 7. DEMO SCENARIO
**Against Camunda 8.9+: do not build it.** The 8.9 audit log answers who did what when, with retention off by
default. A demo claiming "Camunda cannot tell you who decided this" would be **factually wrong** and corrected
in the room. The residual differences (eventual consistency, no hash chain, mutable indices) are too subtle to
carry a demo.

**Against Camunda 7 the gap is real, quotable and permanent** — C7 will never receive the 8.9 audit log and
stopped receiving security patches in Oct 2025:

**a)** `TaskListener` on the approving user task's `complete` event dispatches
`APPROVE_CLAIM { claimId, decision, approverId: task.getAssignee(), decidedAt, ruleVersion, priorState }`.
**b)** Destroy it three ways, all first-party, all traceless: run at the **default `AUDIT` level** and let the
variable row be overwritten in place (*no API call needed — this is what a default install does on its own*);
or `historyService.deleteHistoricProcessInstance(id)`; or let the **mandatory `historyTimeToLive`** expire.
**c)** Replay approver, timestamp, rule version, prior state **and every intermediate value C7 overwrote**.

**Framing caveat:** this lands as a **migration/replacement** argument, not integration — "your system of
record is frozen and unpatched, and it was destroying prior state by default the whole time." Sell to
organisations already forced off C7 by the Oct 2025 EOL who balk at Camunda License 1.0.

---
---

# Tool screen: Flowable

**Researched:** 2026-08-20 · primary sources only
**Verdict: DEAD END** — the slot is occupied and the occupier is procurable

No archival, relicensing or acquisition. `flowable/flowable-engine` live, Apache-2.0, pushed 2026-08-20.

## 3. THE SLOT IS OCCUPIED — and Flowable's own docs draw exactly our distinction
> "Flowable creates a **technical audit trail** (history) by default. When it is required to have a
> **business audit trail**, the audit task is the easiest way to do this."
— https://documentation.flowable.com/latest/reactmodel/bpmn/reference/audit

They shipped it, inside the window — release 2025.2.01, **16 December 2025**:
> "Added support to see the **business audit trail** of a case or process instance."
— https://documentation.flowable.com/latest/admin/release-notes/2025.2.01-release

And they claim immutability, verbatim:
> "**Created *AuditInstances* are immutable.**"
— https://documentation.flowable.com/latest/develop/be/custom-audit

Enterprise `AuditService`: `createAuditInstanceBuilder()` with `creatorId()` (user attribution), `type()`,
`subType()`, `payload()`; stored in `${prefix}flw_audit_instance`; queryable; publishable as an audit stream.

**Is the occupier unprocurable in the EU/German public sector? No — and that decides the lead.**
Flowable AG is **Zurich, Switzerland with a Berlin office**; deployment options are first-party
"Cloud-based / **On-premise** / Hybrid"; certifications SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR; government is a named vertical
(https://www.flowable.com/ai-info-page). A Swiss vendor with a German office, on-prem, ISO 27001 is about as
procurable as these rules get. **No sovereignty exclusion exists.** The remaining objection is price — a
commercial wedge, not a sovereign one.

## 1–2. WHAT IT KEEPS / THE GAP (open-source edition only)
Default history level is `audit`: *"This is the default. It archives all process instances, activity
instances, keeps variable values continuously in sync and all form properties…"*
— https://www.flowable.com/open-source/docs/bpmn/ch10-History

**The decisive finding is mutability, and it comes from the engine's own SQL.** From
`HistoricProcessInstance.xml` (main branch):
```xml
<update id="updateHistoricProcessInstance" ...>
    update ${prefix}ACT_HI_PROCINST
      <set> REV_ = #{revisionNext...},
        <if test="originalPersistentState.startTime != startTime">
          START_TIME_ = #{startTime, jdbcType=TIMESTAMP},
```
**Flowable's own engine issues UPDATE against the history table, with `START_TIME_` rewritable.** The `REV_`
optimistic-locking column is the tell: this row is *designed* to be updated in place.

Six documented deletion methods on `HistoryService` — `deleteHistoricProcessInstance` ("All historic
activities, historic task and historic details … are deleted as well"), `bulkDeleteHistoricProcessInstances`,
`deleteHistoricTaskInstance`, `deleteHistoricTaskLogEntry`, and two `...OfRemovedHistoricProcessInstances`.
There are **no create or update methods** on `HistoryService` — query and delete only.

**Correction to the vault's claim — retention default is favourable to Flowable:**
> "Automatic cleanup of HistoricProcessInstances is **disabled by default**"
Default retention is **infinite**; purging is opt-in (365d / 1AM when enabled).

**Business audit is Enterprise-gated — validated by controlled code search** on
`repo:flowable/flowable-engine`: `AuditService` **0 hits**, `AuditInstance` **0**, `flw_audit_instance` **0**,
against controls `HistoryService` **628** and `HistoricTaskLogEntryBuilder` **31**.

**UNVERIFIED:** async-history defaults; payload truncation limits; Docker pulls; whether `AuditService` sits in
base Case Platform or only the separately-licensed Agentic add-on.

## 4. LICENCE — Apache-2.0, and that cuts both ways
LICENSE verbatim: "Apache License / Version 2.0, January 2004". Engines open; "The commercial platform builds
on those engines and adds enterprise capabilities, governance tooling, and support." No FAQ/repo discrepancy —
Flowable states the split accurately. Apache-2.0 forbids essentially nothing relevant, so Powerhouse can
integrate freely — **and there is no licence-based wedge either.**

## 5. INSTALL BASE
**9,476 GitHub stars / 2,879 forks** (GitHub API 2026-08-20). Vendor first-party, self-reported:
"600+ enterprises worldwide", "Over 1 billion events processed per day". Order of magnitude 10⁴ stars, 10²
named enterprise customers — larger than most of this screen.

## 6. THE SEAM — excellent, and not the problem
`FlowableEventListener` is the right hook:
```java
boolean isFailOnException();
boolean isFireOnTransactionLifecycleEvent();
String getOnTransaction();
```
`getOnTransaction()` allows dispatch **after commit**, so Powerhouse never records a decision Flowable rolled
back; `isFailOnException()` lets the append-only write be a *precondition* of the process advancing. Also
available: `ExecutionListener`, `TaskListener` (prefer `org.flowable.task.service.delegate.TaskListener`).

## 7. DEMO — mutation, not deletion, is the stronger version
**a)** `FlowableEventListener` on `TASK_COMPLETED`, `getOnTransaction()` = COMMITTED, dispatches
`APPROVE_CREDIT_LIMIT { applicantId, priorLimit, newLimit, approverId, ruleVersion, timestamp }`. Note what
the typed operation carries that Flowable's history structurally does not: **prior state** and **rule version**.
**b)** `UPDATE ACT_HI_PROCINST SET START_TIME_='2025-01-01', BUSINESS_KEY_='CASE-9999' WHERE PROC_INST_ID_=?`
— the same statement the engine's own mapper issues.
**c)** Powerhouse replays the original decision.

**What the viewer sees:** Flowable Control re-renders a process that now started in January under a different
business key — no error, no gap, no tamper indicator, `REV_` incremented as if the engine had done it.
**A rewritten history row is indistinguishable from a legitimate one, because legitimate rewrites are how the
engine works.**

**The caption the demo must carry aloud:** this lands against **OSS Flowable only**. It does not land against
Flowable Enterprise `AuditService`.

## VAULT CLAIM: confirmed for OSS, REFUTED as a claim about "Flowable"
The vault says: *"Flowable orchestrates WHEN things happen — the process/case instance is a mutable row and
history is purgeable."*
- **"Mutable row" — confirmed, and more strongly than the workbook knew** (the engine's own UPDATE mapper).
- **"Purgeable" — overstated.** Cleanup is disabled by default; retention is infinite out of the box.
- **Refuted as a claim about Flowable unqualified.** Enterprise ships an immutable business audit trail as of
  2025-12-16. Any pitch asserting Flowable has no immutable business audit log is **factually wrong against
  the commercial product and will be corrected in the room.** The claim must be scoped to the Apache-2.0
  edition in every future use.

---
---

# Tool screen: Alfresco (Community Edition / ACS, Hyland)

**Researched:** 2026-08-20 · primary sources only
**Verdict: PRIMARY** — the best-evidenced gap in this screen

## LEAD: Community Edition is NOT discontinued
The acquisition-decay hypothesis came back negative. `Alfresco/alfresco-community-repo`:
`"archived": false`, `"license": "LGPL-3.0"`, **pushed 2026-08-20** (same day as this research),
**811 commits in 52 weeks**, 196 contributors. CE 25.1 → 25.2 → 25.3 → **26.1 (2026-03-17)** → 26.2 on
schedule. No relicensing. Proceed.

*PARTIALLY VERIFIED (Hyland Connect returned 403; rests on search snippets):* CE 26.1 withdrew supported
Solr search, directing Community users to an effort "not officially supported or maintained by Hyland."
Solr code remains in master — a support/packaging withdrawal, not a code purge. Procurement risk, not a
verified fact.

## 1. WHAT IT KEEPS
Three subsystems, all in LGPL-3.0 Community. Audit lands in three ordinary tables — verbatim DDL:
```sql
CREATE TABLE alf_audit_entry
( id INT8 NOT NULL, audit_app_id INT8 NOT NULL, audit_time INT8 NOT NULL,
  audit_user_id INT8 NULL, audit_values_id INT8 NULL, ...
```
Scope, from the audit application's own header comment:
> "Extracts high level audit records on the creation, deletion, modification and access of **user visible
> objects**."
Docs enumerate it: *"node create, move, delete, aspect add and remove, content read, content update, check
in, check out, cancel"* — every item a document event. Plus `cm:versionable` version history, and the
event bus (`repo.event2.enabled=true` — **on** by default).

## 2. THE GAP — content auditing is OFF by default
The open question from the earlier halted attempt, now **confirmed from two independent primary sources.**
From `repository.properties` (line 289):
```
audit.enabled=true
audit.alfresco-access.enabled=false          ← the one that matters
audit.dod5015.enabled=false
audit.filter.alfresco-access.default.enabled=false
```
`audit.enabled=true` is a decoy — it only arms the framework. The docs are explicit:
> "The auditing system is **disabled by default**, as it has the potential to impact performance"
> "**However, enabling this property does not necessarily result in the generation of audit data.** … you'll
> need to enable the `audit.alfresco-access.enabled` property."

**A default Alfresco Community install records no content audit trail at all.**

**No retention or pruning mechanism exists** — no audit retention property, no automatic policy. Worst of both
worlds for evidence: no defensible expiry policy *and* no protection from manual erasure.

**Deletion, one call, both bounds optional.** From `clear.post.desc.xml`:
> `<url>/api/audit/clear/{application}?fromTime={fromTime}&toTime={toTime}</url>`
> fromTime: "Time … of the oldest audit entry to delete (**omit to assume oldest**)"
> toTime: "Time … of the youngest audit entry to delete (**omit to assume current time**)"

`POST /api/audit/clear/alfresco-access` with no parameters **erases the entire audit history for that
application in a single call.** Also `POST /api/audit/control?enable=false` (disable at runtime, no restart),
`DELETE /api/audit/entries/{id}`, and the v1 REST `DELETE .../audit-entries?where=(...)`.

**Mutability:** the DDL is the whole story — plain `INT8` PK, four FKs, four indexes. **No hash chain, no
previous-row digest, no signature column, no append-only trigger, no CHECK constraint.** A tampered audit
trail is indistinguishable from an untampered one.

**Paid gating: none** — and that's to Alfresco's credit. Audit, all three audit applications and AGS/Records
Management are all in the LGPL-3.0 repo. This is a **design** gap, identical in both editions.

## 3. THE SLOT — nominally filled by AGS, practically empty
Alfresco Governance Services Community is real and in-tree (LGPL-3.0). It does **not** occupy this slot:
1. **It governs record lifecycle, not decisions.** `rm-audit.xml` extractors are `nodeName`, `nodeType`,
   `userRoles`, `namePath`, `nodeRefPath`, `nodeIdentifier` — all node-shaped.
2. **Its audit log is itself erasable** — `DELETE /api/rma/admin/rmauditlog`, whose descriptor declares
   `<authentication>user</authentication>` (not admin). *Effective privilege UNVERIFIED — internal RM
   capability checks in `AuditLogDelete.java` were not read.*
3. **DoD 5015 auditing is off by default.**
4. **Almost nobody deploys it:** 60,006 Docker pulls vs **4,759,526** for the core repository — **1.26%.**

## 4. LICENCE — and the clause that decides it
Community: **LGPL-3.0** ("GNU LESSER GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE / Version 3, 29 June 2007", LICENSE.txt).
Enterprise: proprietary subscription. Two clauses matter, both verbatim from the Alfresco EULA Americas 2021:

> "3.2 Restrictions … (d) **combine, call, link to, or otherwise use the Software in conjunction with any
> Community Version**"

> "3.4 … The Alfresco Content Services (ACS) includes a workflow capability along with a predetermined set of
> document review and approval workflows … **However, User may not use the workflow software to design, create
> or run other types of workflows, business processes and/or management tasks.** A separate subscription for
> Alfresco Process Services (APS) software is required for any such uses."

**Clause 3.4 is a licence-level confirmation of the technical gap.** Under an ACS Enterprise subscription,
modelling your own business process — the decision itself — is **contractually prohibited** without buying a
second product. The gap is not merely unbuilt; **it is licensed shut.**

## 5. INSTALL BASE — 10⁶–10⁷
- `alfresco-content-repository-community`: **4,759,526** Docker pulls
- `alfresco-share`: **6,853,029** pulls
- GitHub: 227 stars / 109 forks / 196 contributors / 811 commits per year

Star count is misleading — enterprise Java ECM is pulled by ops teams, not starred by developers. Docker pulls
are the honest signal. **Trajectory: engineering-healthy, community-thin.** Share has 15 stars; AGS is at 1.26%
of core pulls; `alfresco-event-gateway` now sits under the **`AlfrescoArchive`** org (3 stars, last push
2025-07-12).

## 6. THE SEAM — on by default
`repo.event2` over ActiveMQ: `repo.event2.enabled=true`, `repo.event2.topic.endpoint=amqp:topic:alfresco.repo.event2`.
*(Community limitation, stated in Alfresco's own docs: `resourceReaderAuthorities` ACL fields are
**Enterprise Only**, so Community events are not ACL-filtered.)*

Also in-process `NodeServicePolicies` — and **the interface list is itself the strongest evidence for the
gap**: `OnCreateNodePolicy`, `OnMoveNodePolicy`, `OnUpdatePropertiesPolicy`, `OnAddAspectPolicy`,
`BeforeDeleteNodePolicy`… every extension point is keyed to a *node* verb. There is no `OnDecisionPolicy`, no
`OnApprovalPolicy`, no business-event vocabulary anywhere in the policy surface. You would detect a decision by
*inferring* it from an aspect being added — which is precisely the impedance mismatch.

## 7. DEMO — configured better than default, so it can't be accused of cheating
Enable auditing **fully** (`audit.enabled=true`, `audit.alfresco-access.enabled=true`).

**a)** A grant application is approved. Powerhouse dispatches `ACCEPT_APPLICATION { applicationId, decidedBy,
decidedAt, ruleVersion, priorStatus: "UNDER_REVIEW", newStatus: "ACCEPTED", justification }`. Alfresco
represents the same act as an aspect add plus a property update. Show both: one operation named for the
decision, versus `cm:name` changed and an aspect added.
**b)** One documented admin call, no database access:
```bash
curl -X POST -u admin:admin \
  'http://localhost:8080/alfresco/service/api/audit/clear/alfresco-access'
```
**c)** Powerhouse replays the decision, hash-verified.

**What the viewer sees:** left pane (Alfresco audit query) goes **empty**; right pane unchanged. And **nothing
in Alfresco indicates anything was removed** — no tombstone, no gap marker, no sequence discontinuity, because
`alf_audit_entry` has no integrity constraint to violate. Closing line: *Alfresco can be configured to log that
a file changed; it cannot be configured to prove that a decision was made — and clause 3.4 of its own
Enterprise licence forbids you from building that there without buying a second product.*

## VAULT CLAIM: confirmed, and the vault UNDERSTATES it
The vault says: *"Alfresco records document events — versions, uploads, moves. It does not record the business
decision: who accepted this."* Confirmed three independent ways (audit-app header scope; the enumerated event
list; the node-shaped policy vocabulary). But the correct, stronger claim is:

> *"Alfresco **can** record document events — but only after an administrator explicitly enables the
> alfresco-access audit application, which is **off by default**. It never records the business decision. And
> whatever it does record sits in an ordinary mutable table that a single documented API call can erase in
> full."*

# Tool screen: ERPNext / Frappe Framework

**Question set:** seven-question integration-gap screen for Powerhouse
**Researched:** 2026-08-19 · primary sources only · by knowledge-agent
**Scope note:** ERPNext (the ERP application) and Frappe Framework (the platform beneath it) are
**separately licensed** and are treated separately below where it matters.

---

## LEAD: corporate status in the last 24 months

Frappe is an **acquirer, not a target**. Frappe Technologies acquired **The Commit Company on 1 January
2026**, with the team joining Frappe and "all existing products and libraries being moved to the Frappe
GitHub repository."
Source: https://thecommit.company/blog/company/announcing-our-acquisition-by-frappe

No relicensing or archival found. This resolves — in the opposite direction — an unverified "acquisition
lead" raised earlier in this research.

---

## 1. WHAT IT DOES KEEP

Frappe maintains change history in the **`Version` DocType**. When `track_changes` is enabled on a DocType,
every save creates a Version record capturing "the additions, deletions, and modifications made during that
specific save instance."
Source: https://docs.frappe.io/erpnext/user/manual/en/document-versioning

Alongside it sit ordinary logging DocTypes — Error Log, Activity Log, Route History — governed by a
**Log Settings** DocType which "lets you configure retention period for default logging doctypes."
Source: https://docs.frappe.io/framework/user/en/logging

**Storage form:** all of these are ordinary DocTypes, i.e. **rows in the relational database**
(`tabVersion` etc.). They are not an append-only stream and carry no documented hash or chain.

---

## 2. WHAT IT DOES NOT KEEP — the gap

**There is no immutable, user-attributed, append-only log of business events on by default.** Four
independent findings:

**(a) Tracking is opt-in, per DocType.** Versioning is enabled by ticking "Track changes" in Customize Form:
> "Go to Purchase Order List. Click on Customize from the drop-down menu... Check the field 'Track changes'
> in the Properties."
Source: https://docs.frappe.io/erpnext/user/manual/en/document-versioning
A business event on an untracked DocType leaves no Version record at all.

**(b) Deleting the document destroys its history — the decisive finding.** On delete, Frappe removes the
document's Version references:
> `delete_references("Version", doctype, name, "ref_doctype", "docname")`
Source: https://github.com/frappe/frappe/blob/develop/frappe/model/delete_doc.py
**The audit trail dies with the record it audits.** An append-only log must outlive its subject; this one
does not.

**(c) Records are mutable rows.** Version entries are ordinary DocType rows in MariaDB/Postgres, reachable by
`frappe.delete_doc` (the document `delete()` method "is an alias to `frappe.delete_doc`",
https://frappeframework.com/docs/user/en/api/document) and by any direct SQL `UPDATE`. Nothing in the
documentation asserts immutability, hashing or tamper-evidence.

**(d) Retention is a pruning system by design.** "Most logging doctypes in Frappe support configurable
retention period with sane defaults", cleared on a scheduled basis.
Source: https://docs.frappe.io/framework/user/en/logging

**Paid gating:** none found. The capability is not withheld behind a paid tier — it simply is not an
append-only business log. This is a design boundary, not an upsell.

**UNVERIFIED:** the exact numeric default retention for each logging DocType (the docs say "sane defaults"
without listing them; a 180-day figure appears only as a code example for *custom* logging doctypes);
whether `Version` is itself registered for automatic clearing by default; and whether Frappe Cloud offers
any audit capability beyond the self-hosted product.

---

## 3. IS THE SLOT ALREADY OCCUPIED?

**No — not for this gap.** Frappe does ship a first-party feature literally called **Audit Trail**, so this
required checking. It is narrower than its name:
> "A tool for viewing the changes made to a submittable doctype across multiple amended versions" — tracking
> "Fields Changed", "Rows Updated", "Rows Added / Rows Removed".
Source: https://docs.frappe.io/framework/user/en/audit-trail

That is a **diff viewer over amendments of submittable documents**, not an immutable attributed log of
business decisions. The page makes no claim of default-on behaviour, immutability, hashing, chaining or
deletion protection. No vendor announcement in the last 24 months was found that closes the gap — the one
material corporate event is Frappe *acquiring* a developer-tooling company (see LEAD).

No sovereignty wedge is required, because the slot is open.

---

## 4. LICENCE REALITY

Two repositories, two licences — the distinction matters:

| component | licence (as stated in the repo) | source |
|---|---|---|
| **ERPNext** (application) | **GPL-3.0** | https://github.com/frappe/erpnext |
| **Frappe Framework** (platform) | **MIT** | https://github.com/frappe/frappe |

Both are genuine OSI-approved open source. **No open-core split was found on the audit capability** — unlike
the open-core vendors elsewhere in this corpus, there is no Enterprise edition withholding the audit feature.
GPL-3.0 on ERPNext is copyleft and reciprocal, which is compatible with Powerhouse's own AGPL-3.0 posture and
unproblematic for public-sector procurement. MIT on the framework is permissive.

No discrepancy found between vendor FAQ and repo.

---

## 5. INSTALL BASE — order of magnitude

- **ERPNext: 38.3k GitHub stars** (github.com/frappe/erpnext, retrieved 2026-08-19)

**`doc_events` in `hooks.py`** — a documented, first-class controller-hook mechanism, with wildcard support

## 7. THE DEMO SCENARIO

**a) Dispatch a typed operation at the decision point.** Register `doc_events` on `on_submit` for
Purchase Order (or Sales Invoice). Submitting the document — the moment of business approval — dispatches a
typed, user-attributed operation to Powerhouse recording who submitted it, when, and the state at submission.

**b) Destroy the record in ERPNext.** Delete the Purchase Order. Frappe's `delete_doc` cascades
`delete_references("Version", doctype, name, ...)`, so the document **and its entire version history**
disappear together. Optionally also demonstrate mutation: a direct `UPDATE` on `tabVersion` alters the
"audit" record silently, since it is an ordinary row.

**c) Replay the business decision from Powerhouse.** The append-only record still answers who approved the
purchase order, when, and under which rule.

**What the viewer sees in under 60 seconds:** the approval exists in ERPNext; the document is deleted; ERPNext
can no longer answer *who approved it* — the version history went with the record — while Powerhouse replays
the approval chain intact. The point being proved is not that ERPNext is careless, but that **its history is
scoped to the lifetime of the row**, and a decision record must outlive the thing it describes.

# Tool screen: n8n

**Researched:** 2026-08-20 · primary sources only
**Verdict: PRIMARY** — with two independent wedges (technical gap + procurement licence)

## LEAD: corporate status
No relicensing, no acquisition. Live `LICENSE.md` still reads "Sustainable Use License / Version 1.0"
(created 2022, unchanged). Independent, Berlin HQ.
*UNVERIFIED-primary (secondary press only): $180M Series C at $2.5B post-money, Oct 2025; >$40M ARR;
3,000+ enterprise customers.*

## 1. WHAT IT KEEPS
Two ordinary TypeORM SQL tables. `execution_entity` holds metadata (`id`, `status`, `mode`, `createdAt`,
`startedAt`) and imports `DeleteDateColumn` — soft delete. `execution_data` holds the payload as **a single
`text` blob**, cascade-deleted with its parent:
```ts
@Column('text') data: string;
@OneToOne('ExecutionEntity', 'executionData', { onDelete: 'CASCADE' })
```
Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/n8n-io/n8n/master/packages/@n8n/db/src/entities/execution-data.ts ·
.../execution-entity.ts

Event log file: "By default, n8n writes the event log to `<n8n-user-folder>/n8nEventLog.log`"
— https://docs.n8n.io/administer/observe-and-log/stream-logs-to-external-systems.md

## 2. THE GAP — decisive: it forgets by default
**Being fair first:** `EXECUTIONS_DATA_SAVE_ON_SUCCESS` defaults to `all`, so n8n *does* record runs. The gap
is that it then **deletes them on a timer**, and what it records is not a business record.

| variable | **shipped default** |
|---|---|
| `EXECUTIONS_DATA_PRUNE` | **`true`** |
| `EXECUTIONS_DATA_MAX_AGE` | **`336` hours = 14 days** |
| `EXECUTIONS_DATA_PRUNE_MAX_COUNT` | `10000` |
| `EXECUTIONS_DATA_MAX_DISPLAY_SIZE` | `104857600` (100 MB, truncates display) |

> "n8n enables pruning by default" … prunes when **either** "**Age**: The execution finished more than
> `EXECUTIONS_DATA_MAX_AGE` hours ago" or the count exceeds `PRUNE_MAX_COUNT`, removing "finished executions
> along with their execution data and binary data."
— https://docs.n8n.io/deploy/host-n8n/configure-n8n/scaling/manage-execution-data ·
https://docs.n8n.io/deploy/host-n8n/configure-n8n/basic-configuration/use-environment-variables/executions

**Deletion API:** `DELETE /api/v1/executions/{id}` — "Deletes an execution from your instance."
https://docs.n8n.io/connect/n8n-api/execution.md

**Mutability:** ordinary Postgres/SQLite/MySQL rows behind TypeORM. No hash, no signature, no chain, no
append-only constraint in either entity. Anyone with DB credentials can `UPDATE execution_data SET data = ...`
undetected.

**No user attribution on the decision.** `mode` is an enum (`webhook`, `trigger`, `manual`, `cli`, `retry`).
An execution is attributed to a **workflow**, never to a deciding human under a rule.

**The `/audit` endpoint is not an audit log — it is a vulnerability scanner:**
> `"summary":"Generate an audit","description":"Generate a security audit for your n8n instance."` returning
> "Credentials Risk Report", "Database Risk Report", "Filesystem Risk Report", "Nodes Risk Report"
— https://docs.n8n.io/connect/n8n-api/audit.md

**Audit events that do exist are identity/admin only** — login, signup, credentials, MFA, package installed,
`User execution deleted`, `Execution data revealed`. Nothing about *what was decided*.

**Paid gating, stated twice independently:**
> "Log Streaming is available on: **n8n Cloud:** Enterprise • **Self-hosted:** Enterprise"
> "The Community edition … doesn't include these features: … Log streaming"
— https://docs.n8n.io/administer/observe-and-log/stream-logs-to-external-systems.md ·
https://docs.n8n.io/deploy/host-n8n/community-edition-features.md

Note the irony: **"User execution deleted" is itself only observable through the Enterprise-only channel.**

## 1–2. WHAT IT KEEPS / THE GAP, per edition

**Camunda 7 — gap real, quotable, permanent.** Default history level is `AUDIT`. The decisive line:
> "Rows in this table are **updated** as variable instances are updated, meaning that **only the last value
> of a process variable will be available**."
— https://docs.camunda.org/manual/7.24/user-guide/process-engine/history/history-configuration/

Destructive in-place update, not an append-only log. Prior state is gone unless you opt up to `FULL` (which is

Deletion is designed in:
> "**The history time to live is mandatory**, any deployment or re-deployment of any model resource (BPMN, DMN,
> CMMN) that contains a historyTimeToLive of null **will be prevented**."
— https://docs.camunda.org/manual/7.24/user-guide/process-engine/history/history-cleanup/

**Camunda 7.24 refuses to deploy a process model until you declare when its history will be destroyed.**

Explicit APIs: `HistoryService.deleteHistoricProcessInstance(id)` ("Deletes historic process instance along
with all historic activities, historic task and historic details"), `...IfExists`, and bulk
`deleteHistoricProcessInstancesAsync(query, reason)`. No hash chain, no tamper evidence.

**Camunda 8 — mostly closed.** Retention ships **disabled** (`retention.enabled: false`, `minimum-age: 30d`) —
a genuine point in Camunda's favour. Residual gaps: records are ordinary mutable Elasticsearch/OpenSearch
documents (integrity protection *absent* — INFERRED, no source claims one exists), and the 8.9 audit log is
"Eventually Consistent" per its own API spec, so not transactionally coupled to the decision it records.

`FlowableEventListener` is the right hook:
```java

boolean isFireOnTransactionLifecycleEvent();
String getOnTransaction();
```
`getOnTransaction()` allows dispatch **after commit**, so Powerhouse never records a decision Flowable rolled
back; `isFailOnException()` lets the append-only write be a *precondition* of the process advancing. Also

- **"Purgeable" — overstated.** Cleanup is disabled by default; retention is infinite out of the box.
- **Refuted as a claim about Flowable unqualified.** Enterprise ships an immutable business audit trail as of
  2025-12-16. Any pitch asserting Flowable has no immutable business audit log is **factually wrong against
  the commercial product and will be corrected in the room.** The claim must be scoped to the Apache-2.0
  edition in every future use.

---
---

# Tool screen: Alfresco (Community Edition / ACS, Hyland)

**Researched:** 2026-08-20 · primary sources only
**Verdict: PRIMARY** — the best-evidenced gap in this screen

## LEAD: Community Edition is NOT discontinued
The acquisition-decay hypothesis came back negative. `Alfresco/alfresco-community-repo`:
`"archived": false`, `"license": "LGPL-3.0"`, **pushed 2026-08-20** (same day as this research),
**811 commits in 52 weeks**, 196 contributors. CE 25.1 → 25.2 → 25.3 → **26.1 (2026-03-17)** → 26.2 on
schedule. No relicensing. Proceed.

*PARTIALLY VERIFIED (Hyland Connect returned 403; rests on search snippets):* CE 26.1 withdrew supported
Solr search, directing Community users to an effort "not officially supported or maintained by Hyland."
Solr code remains in master — a support/packaging withdrawal, not a code purge. Procurement risk, not a
verified fact.

## 1. WHAT IT KEEPS
Three subsystems, all in LGPL-3.0 Community. Audit lands in three ordinary tables — verbatim DDL:
```sql
CREATE TABLE alf_audit_entry
( id INT8 NOT NULL, audit_app_id INT8 NOT NULL, audit_time INT8 NOT NULL,
  audit_user_id INT8 NULL, audit_values_id INT8 NULL, ...
```
Scope, from the audit application's own header comment:
> "Extracts high level audit records on the creation, deletion, modification and access of **user visible
> objects**."
Docs enumerate it: *"node create, move, delete, aspect add and remove, content read, content update, check
in, check out, cancel"* — every item a document event. Plus `cm:versionable` version history, and the
event bus (`repo.event2.enabled=true` — **on** by default).

## 2. THE GAP — content auditing is OFF by default
The open question from the earlier halted attempt, now **confirmed from two independent primary sources.**
From `repository.properties` (line 289):
```
audit.enabled=true
audit.alfresco-access.enabled=false          ← the one that matters
audit.dod5015.enabled=false
audit.filter.alfresco-access.default.enabled=false
```
`audit.enabled=true` is a decoy — it only arms the framework. The docs are explicit:
> "The auditing system is **disabled by default**, as it has the potential to impact performance"
> "**However, enabling this property does not necessarily result in the generation of audit data.** … you'll
> need to enable the `audit.alfresco-access.enabled` property."

**A default Alfresco Community install records no content audit trail at all.**

**No retention or pruning mechanism exists** — no audit retention property, no automatic policy. Worst of both
worlds for evidence: no defensible expiry policy *and* no protection from manual erasure.

**Deletion, one call, both bounds optional.** From `clear.post.desc.xml`:
> `<url>/api/audit/clear/{application}?fromTime={fromTime}&toTime={toTime}</url>`
> fromTime: "Time … of the oldest audit entry to delete (**omit to assume oldest**)"
> toTime: "Time … of the youngest audit entry to delete (**omit to assume current time**)"

`POST /api/audit/clear/alfresco-access` with no parameters **erases the entire audit history for that
application in a single call.** Also `POST /api/audit/control?enable=false` (disable at runtime, no restart),
`DELETE /api/audit/entries/{id}`, and the v1 REST `DELETE .../audit-entries?where=(...)`.

**Mutability:** the DDL is the whole story — plain `INT8` PK, four FKs, four indexes. **No hash chain, no
previous-row digest, no signature column, no append-only trigger, no CHECK constraint.** A tampered audit
trail is indistinguishable from an untampered one.

**Paid gating: none** — and that's to Alfresco's credit. Audit, all three audit applications and AGS/Records
Management are all in the LGPL-3.0 repo. This is a **design** gap, identical in both editions.

## 3. THE SLOT — nominally filled by AGS, practically empty
Alfresco Governance Services Community is real and in-tree (LGPL-3.0). It does **not** occupy this slot:
1. **It governs record lifecycle, not decisions.** `rm-audit.xml` extractors are `nodeName`, `nodeType`,
   `userRoles`, `namePath`, `nodeRefPath`, `nodeIdentifier` — all node-shaped.
2. **Its audit log is itself erasable** — `DELETE /api/rma/admin/rmauditlog`, whose descriptor declares
   `<authentication>user</authentication>` (not admin). *Effective privilege UNVERIFIED — internal RM
   capability checks in `AuditLogDelete.java` were not read.*
3. **DoD 5015 auditing is off by default.**
4. **Almost nobody deploys it:** 60,006 Docker pulls vs **4,759,526** for the core repository — **1.26%.**

## 4. LICENCE — and the clause that decides it
Community: **LGPL-3.0** ("GNU LESSER GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE / Version 3, 29 June 2007", LICENSE.txt).
Enterprise: proprietary subscription. Two clauses matter, both verbatim from the Alfresco EULA Americas 2021:

> "3.2 Restrictions … (d) **combine, call, link to, or otherwise use the Software in conjunction with any
> Community Version**"

> "3.4 … The Alfresco Content Services (ACS) includes a workflow capability along with a predetermined set of
> document review and approval workflows … **However, User may not use the workflow software to design, create
> or run other types of workflows, business processes and/or management tasks.** A separate subscription for
> Alfresco Process Services (APS) software is required for any such uses."

**Clause 3.4 is a licence-level confirmation of the technical gap.** Under an ACS Enterprise subscription,
modelling your own business process — the decision itself — is **contractually prohibited** without buying a
second product. The gap is not merely unbuilt; **it is licensed shut.**

## 5. INSTALL BASE — 10⁶–10⁷
- `alfresco-content-repository-community`: **4,759,526** Docker pulls
- `alfresco-share`: **6,853,029** pulls
- GitHub: 227 stars / 109 forks / 196 contributors / 811 commits per year

Star count is misleading — enterprise Java ECM is pulled by ops teams, not starred by developers. Docker pulls
are the honest signal. **Trajectory: engineering-healthy, community-thin.** Share has 15 stars; AGS is at 1.26%
of core pulls; `alfresco-event-gateway` now sits under the **`AlfrescoArchive`** org (3 stars, last push
2025-07-12).

## 6. THE SEAM — on by default
`repo.event2` over ActiveMQ: `repo.event2.enabled=true`, `repo.event2.topic.endpoint=amqp:topic:alfresco.repo.event2`.
*(Community limitation, stated in Alfresco's own docs: `resourceReaderAuthorities` ACL fields are
**Enterprise Only**, so Community events are not ACL-filtered.)*

Also in-process `NodeServicePolicies` — and **the interface list is itself the strongest evidence for the
gap**: `OnCreateNodePolicy`, `OnMoveNodePolicy`, `OnUpdatePropertiesPolicy`, `OnAddAspectPolicy`,
`BeforeDeleteNodePolicy`… every extension point is keyed to a *node* verb. There is no `OnDecisionPolicy`, no
`OnApprovalPolicy`, no business-event vocabulary anywhere in the policy surface. You would detect a decision by
*inferring* it from an aspect being added — which is precisely the impedance mismatch.

## 7. DEMO — configured better than default, so it can't be accused of cheating
Enable auditing **fully** (`audit.enabled=true`, `audit.alfresco-access.enabled=true`).

**a)** A grant application is approved. Powerhouse dispatches `ACCEPT_APPLICATION { applicationId, decidedBy,
decidedAt, ruleVersion, priorStatus: "UNDER_REVIEW", newStatus: "ACCEPTED", justification }`. Alfresco
represents the same act as an aspect add plus a property update. Show both: one operation named for the
decision, versus `cm:name` changed and an aspect added.
**b)** One documented admin call, no database access:
```bash
curl -X POST -u admin:admin \
  'http://localhost:8080/alfresco/service/api/audit/clear/alfresco-access'
```
**c)** Powerhouse replays the decision, hash-verified.

**What the viewer sees:** left pane (Alfresco audit query) goes **empty**; right pane unchanged. And **nothing
in Alfresco indicates anything was removed** — no tombstone, no gap marker, no sequence discontinuity, because
`alf_audit_entry` has no integrity constraint to violate. Closing line: *Alfresco can be configured to log that
a file changed; it cannot be configured to prove that a decision was made — and clause 3.4 of its own
Enterprise licence forbids you from building that there without buying a second product.*

## VAULT CLAIM: confirmed, and the vault UNDERSTATES it
The vault says: *"Alfresco records document events — versions, uploads, moves. It does not record the business
decision: who accepted this."* Confirmed three independent ways (audit-app header scope; the enumerated event
list; the node-shaped policy vocabulary). But the correct, stronger claim is:

> *"Alfresco **can** record document events — but only after an administrator explicitly enables the
> alfresco-access audit application, which is **off by default**. It never records the business decision. And
> whatever it does record sits in an ordinary mutable table that a single documented API call can erase in
> full."*

---
---

# Tool screen: Odoo

**Researched:** 2026-08-20 · primary sources only
**Verdict: COMPETITOR** — the slot is filled, in the free edition, by default

## LEAD: the brief's hypothesis is refuted by the code
The decisive question was "is the Audit Trail Community or Enterprise?" **It is Community.** It lives in
`addons/account` inside `odoo/odoo` under **LGPL-3** (`__manifest__.py`: `'license': 'LGPL-3'`), and Odoo 19
turned it on for everyone:
> "The non-restrictive audit trail has been **made available by default for everyone**."
— https://www.odoo.com/odoo-19-release-notes

Code search confirms: `audit_trail repo:odoo/odoo` → 19 files, all in the LGPL repo. There is no
`account_audit_trail` module and no audit module among the 636 Community addons.

**So the open-core sovereignty wedge does not exist here.** No archival, relicensing or acquisition either
(`pushed_at: 2026-08-20`, `archived: false`); the LGPL relicensing everyone cites was Odoo 9, in 2015.

## 3. THE SLOT IS OCCUPIED — and in Germany it is *forced* on
> "The :guilabel:`Audit Trail` report tracks changes made to fields that have an impact on accounting and
> includes the date and time of the changes, **the user who made the changes**, the type of change, the
> previous value, and the updated value."
> "An optional **restrictive mode** prevents tracked records from being deleted for more controlled
> immutability. Instead of being deleted, these records can only be cancelled or archived."

`addons/l10n_de/models/res_company.py` forces it for German companies:
```python
company.force_restrictive_audit_trail |= company.country_code == 'DE'
```
and `addons/account/models/company.py` makes that undisableable:
```python
raise ValidationError(_("Can't disable restricted audit trail: forced by localization."))
```
German fiscal docs: *"Odoo is certified **GoBD-compliant**"* … *"**Inalterability** | With the German Odoo
localization, Odoo is in standard configured in such a way that the inalterability clause can be adhered to
without any further customization."*

Plus a real hash chain (`data_inalterability.rst`): SHA-256 over `name`, `date`, `journal_id`, `company_id`,
`debit`, `credit`, `account_id`, `partner_id`, and *"the previous entry's hash is always added to the next
entry to form a hash chain."* Note the scope: it hashes **8 accounting field values**, not the decision, the
rule applied, or the rationale.

## 1–2. WHAT IT KEEPS / THE RESIDUAL GAP
`mail.tracking.value` — ordinary PostgreSQL rows, one per changed field, hung off `mail.message` with
`ondelete='cascade'`. Attribution exists, per Odoo's own German docs: *"Each record in Odoo is stamped with the
creator of the document, the creation date, the modification date, and who modified it."*

The residual gap is **narrow but real and quotable**:
- **`tracking=True` is opt-in per field.** `_track_get_fields` filters on `getattr(field, 'tracking', None)` —
  absent attribute → untracked. Nothing is tracked unless a developer opted that field in.
- **Restrictive (deletion-preventing) mode is OFF by default** — `restrictive_audit_trail` is declared with no
  `default=True`; so is `restrict_mode_hash_table`.
- **Protection covers only 5 models and only `message_type == 'tracking'`.** The `DOMAINS` dict in
  `addons/account/models/mail_message.py` holds exactly `res.company`, `account.move`, `account.account`,
  `account.tax`, `res.partner`. **Everything else has zero deletion protection** — purchase approvals, expense
  approvals, HR decisions, grant awards, permission grants.
- **Every internal employee can delete the record.** `addons/mail/security/ir.model.access.csv`:
  `access_mail_message_user,...,base.group_user,1,1,1,1` — read/write/create/**unlink** for
  `base.group_user`, i.e. every internal user. And the cascade takes the field diffs with it.
- **Three documented kill switches:** `tracking_disable`, `mail_notrack`, and a blessed `bypass_audit` token.
- **A first-class sanctioned bypass model:** `account.lock_exception`, whose `reason` is a nullable `Char`,
  which applies to everyone if `user_id` is null and lasts forever if `end_datetime` is null.
- **NO retention gap — reported honestly.** `mail.message` has no pruning cron; the only default GC is on
  *notifications* (`_gc_notifications(max_age_days=180)`). **Do not pitch retention as a gap here.**

Worth noting in Odoo's favour: `mail_thread.py` *does* block editing — *"Messages with tracking values cannot
be modified"* — so the weakness is deletion, not mutation.

## 4. LICENCE
Community **LGPL-3** (LICENSE verbatim; GitHub's detector reports `NOASSERTION` because the file is composite).
Enterprise under the Odoo Enterprise Edition License v1.0: *"can only be used … with a valid Odoo Enterprise
Subscription"* and *"**It is forbidden to publish, distribute, sublicense, or sell copies**"*. A third bucket,
Odoo Apps, sits under the Odoo Proprietary License v1.0. **Audit falls entirely on the LGPL side** —
`account`, `mail`, `base_automation`, `rpc` are all LGPL-3.

## 5. INSTALL BASE — tens of millions of seats
53,814 stars / 33,473 forks; **52,838,592 Docker Hub pulls** (`library/odoo`), all 2026-08-20. Self-reported:
*"over 28,000,000 users worldwide"*, "21,000+" partners, "50,000+ apps".
**The brief's "12 million users" figure is STALE.** ⚠️ The 28M is marketing self-report with no methodology —
primary in source, not in rigour. Docker pulls and stars are machine-verifiable; the seat count is not.

## 6. THE SEAM — clean, and all LGPL Community
The best path is an **outgoing webhook server action**, `ir.actions.server` with `state='webhook'`:
`webhook_url` plus `webhook_field_ids`, where *"The id and model of the record are always sent as '_id' and
'_model'. The name of the action that triggered the webhook is always sent as '_name'."* Driven by a
`base.automation` rule on a state transition — a typed event at the decision point, **with no Odoo source
changes**. Also available: incoming webhooks (`POST /web/hook/<uuid>`, Odoo 17+), ORM `write()`/`create()`
overrides, and the new JSON-2 external API (`POST /json/2/<model>/<method>`).
*Procurement caveat, quoted:* external API access "is only available on *Custom* Odoo pricing plans" — that
gate is Odoo Online SaaS only; self-hosted Community has no such restriction.

## 7. DEMO — if you keep Odoo at all, this is the only honest version
The gap is **not** "Odoo has no audit trail". It is that **immutability stops at the edge of the five-model
`DOMAINS` dict, and inside it every employee holds `unlink`.**

**a)** `base.automation` on `purchase.order`, trigger `on_write` of `state → 'purchase'`, action = webhook
server action → Powerhouse records `APPROVE_PURCHASE_ORDER` (actor, timestamp, threshold applied, prior state).
**b)** As a plain employee — not admin — `POST /json/2/mail.message/unlink` on the chatter tracking message.
**It succeeds silently:** `purchase.order` is absent from `DOMAINS`, so `_except_audit_log()` returns without
raising; `base.group_user` has unlink; the cascade removes the field diffs.
**c)** Powerhouse replays the approval intact.

**The honest second beat that makes it credible rather than a strawman:** run the identical `unlink` against a
posted `account.move` at a German company. Odoo raises *"You cannot remove parts of a restricted audit trail.
Archive the record instead."* That draws the boundary on screen — **Odoo defends the books, and only the books.**

## VAULT CLAIM: first half confirmed, second half REFUTED
The vault says: *"Odoo IS the system of record for what it covers — so the fit is NOT 'a second database'. It
is field-level attribution."*
- **"System of record" — CONFIRMED.** GoBD-certified; German tax authorities treat the Odoo database as the
  statutory books. Powerhouse should not try to be a parallel ledger.
- **"Field-level attribution" — REFUTED as a Powerhouse opportunity.** That seam is already occupied, in
  LGPL-3, by default since Odoo 19. Odoo's own docs describe exactly it: *"it can be seen which value was
  changed by whom in the chatter of the relevant object."*

**Consequence: drop the field-level-attribution pitch.** Keep Odoo as an integration/partner story via the
webhook seam if at all. The workbook was right about the framing and wrong about the seam.
